title: 六月二十七日望湖楼醉书·其一
titlePy: Liùyuè Èrshíqī Rì Wànghú Lóu Zuì Shū · Qí Yī
titleEn: Written Tipsy at Lake View Tower on the 27th Day of the Sixth Month (No. 1)
author: 苏轼
intro: A summer storm on West Lake, start to finish, in four lines: black clouds, rain bouncing like pearls, a wind that sweeps it all away — and calm water as wide as the sky.
analysis: 这首诗写西湖上的一场夏天的急雨，四句写了四个画面。第一句：乌云像打翻的墨汁一样涌上来，还没把山完全遮住；第二句：白亮的雨点像珍珠一样蹦跳着，乱纷纷地落进船里。“翻墨”写云的颜色和来势，“跳珠”写雨点的样子和声音，比喻非常生动。第三句：忽然一阵大风贴着地面卷来，把乌云和雨一下子吹散了；第四句：望湖楼下的湖水平静下来，水天一色，好像天空一样广阔。从云来、雨落，到风起、雨停，一场雨来得快、去得也快，诗人用短短二十八个字写得清清楚楚。最后一句的平静和前面的急骤形成对比，让人感到雨后天地格外清新开阔。
analysisEn: A sudden summer shower on West Lake, told in four quick pictures. First: black clouds pour in like spilled ink, though they haven’t yet covered the hills. Second: white rain bounces like pearls and scatters wildly into the boat. “Spilled ink” gives both the colour of the clouds and the way they surge across the sky; “jumping pearls” gives both the look and the sound of the raindrops — two vivid comparisons. Third: a wind rolls in along the ground and suddenly blows the whole storm away. Fourth: below Lake View Tower, the water lies calm and broad, as wide and bright as the sky itself. Clouds, rain, wind, calm: the storm comes fast and goes fast, and Su Shi catches all of it in twenty-eight characters. The stillness of the last line, set against the rush of the first three, makes the washed, open world after the rain feel especially fresh. The title adds that he was a little drunk — which may explain the delight.
background: Su Shi (1037–1101), also called Su Dongpo, was serving as deputy prefect of Hangzhou when he wrote this in 1072. Lake View Tower stood on the shore of West Lake; he wrote a set of five poems there, and this is the first.
version: 采用统编小学语文教材版本。原作共五首，这是第一首。

lines.py: hēi yún fān mò wèi zhē shān
lines.lit: Black clouds, like spilled ink, have not yet covered the hills;
lines.en: Black clouds spill like ink, but the hills still show;

lines.py: bái yǔ tiào zhū luàn rù chuán
lines.lit: white rain, jumping pearls, scatters into the boat.
lines.en: white rain bounces like pearls all over the boat.

lines.py: juǎn dì fēng lái hū chuī sàn
lines.lit: A ground-sweeping wind comes and suddenly blows it apart;
lines.en: Then a wind sweeps over the ground and blows it all away —

lines.py: wàng hú lóu xià shuǐ rú tiān
lines.lit: below Lake View Tower, the water is like the sky.
lines.en: below the tower, the lake lies wide and clear as the sky.

words.en: Lake View Tower (on West Lake, Hangzhou)

words.note: 书：写。现代汉语“书写”“书法”。
翻：打翻。形容乌云又黑又浓、来得快。
急雨在光下发白，现代汉语不这么说。

words.en: a wind sweeping along the ground
words.note: 现代汉语“席卷”“风卷残云”。

words.en: the water is like the sky
words.note: 形容湖面平静开阔，倒映天空。

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 乌云像打翻的墨，写出暴雨来得急、来势猛。
imagery.en: Clouds like spilled ink show how suddenly and fiercely the storm arrives.

imagery.name: 雨
imagery.zh: 雨点像跳动的珍珠，有声有色，热闹而短暂。
imagery.en: Raindrops bouncing like pearls — loud, bright and brief.

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 卷地而来的风一下子吹散云雨，是天气转变的关键。
imagery.en: The sweeping wind clears the storm in a moment — the turning point.

imagery.name: 西湖
imagery.zh: 雨后的西湖水天一色，平静开阔。
imagery.en: After the rain, West Lake and the sky blend into one calm, open expanse.
